notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My tool for searching and reading web pages was cut off at its usage limit before any pages loaded, so I didn't read a single source.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and leave out anything I couldn't find. With no pages read, every section would be empty. I haven't written notes from memory, because that would break the rule about never filling gaps from my own knowledge.

These are the pages I tried to load. You can open them yourself, or ask me again when the tool is available:

- **Enduring Word (David Guzik):** https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-47/
- **Gill:** https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/psalms/47.htm
- **Ellicott:** https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/psalms/47.htm
- **Pulpit Commentary:** https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/psalms/47.htm
- **Precept Austin:** https://www.preceptaustin.org/psalm-47-commentary
- **NET Bible notes:** https://netbible.org/bible/Psalms+47
- **Augustine's commentary (Catholic and early church view):** https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/1801046.htm. Augustine used the Latin Bible, where this psalm is numbered 46, so his Psalm 47 is a different psalm.

Next time I'd also search Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (spurgeon.org), Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Matthew Henry (ccel.org) and the Lutheran site lcms.org. I'd look at verse 5 in particular ("God has ascended..."), which church teachers often link to Christ's ascension. I'd only include what those pages actually say.
